name: Papal States (1808–1825)
description: A white field with the crossed keys of Saint Peter, one gold and one silver, tied with a red cord and surmounted by the papal tiara.
history: First white flag of the Papal States, introduced in 1808 by Pius VII with the keys and tiara of the Holy See; white and yellow replaced the older red and yellow. From 1825 the flag was divided vertically white and yellow with the arms on the white, the form used until the fall of Rome in 1870.
